title: RAW accidental form requires substantial form while preparation and manifestation keep separate scopes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Complete Steele81 distinguishes being-giving form from dependent accidental form, conditions reception on prepared matter, and denies separate visible matter/form. Retain the full generation, diversity and Trinity argument; no symmetric dependence or modern ontology is silently supplied.

design.mechanism: The full matter/form paragraph distinguishes essential form, which perfects matter and gives a thing being, from accidental form, which does not give being and requires a substantial form. It also makes material disposition a condition of receiving form, with earth-to-fire preparation as example, and ends by distinguishing conceptual priority from visibility: matter is never seen without form, nor form in act without matter. This written prerequisite direction and these reciprocal manifestation claims must coexist with the paragraph's generation, diversity and Trinity statements rather than being flattened into interchangeable labels.
design.contrast: R1: accidental form independently gives a thing substantial being. R2: substantial form depends on an accidental form merely because the latter requires the former. R3: any unprepared material receives any form equally. R4: conceptual distinction entails separate visible instances of pure matter or form. R5: common/general matter must also be directly known because it causes visible made things. R6: the paragraph's matter-based and form-based diversity claims are silently rewritten as one modern taxonomy or its theological example is deleted.
design.prediction: A faithful whole-content account must keep accidental form dependent without granting it the being-giving role assigned to essential form, preserve the material-preparation condition and the closing reciprocal limits on separate visibility, and retain the other generation/diversity claims. Reversing the prerequisite or promoting an accidental attribute to the source of being changes the account; treating a conceptual distinction as a visible separation contradicts its final sentences. Relative elementary classification in594 and mere appearance change in593 do not alone state these whole duties.
whole_source_duties: Full paragraph81: matter and form are principles of bodily things; their privation is described as destruction. Preserve this opening scope rather than treating it as a physical operation performed on a named object.
Subtler/higher matter is more able to receive form/shape; thicker/earthly matter is weaker in reception. This is a qualitative comparison, not a measured universal material parameter.

Matter is named as a principle of distinction, diversity, multiplication and generated things; generating and generated differ with respect to matter. Generation without matter is then said to share substance/kind, illustrated by persons of the Trinity. The theological analogy is an explicit whole-paragraph duty, not independent evidence or a claim about target imagery.

Form also supplies diversity between things. Keep both matter- and form-associated difference claims; do not silently assign individual-versus-species senses that the passage does not explicitly specify.

Essential form enters matter, perfects it and gives the thing being. The subsequent when form is destroyed clause appears within this discussion; its exact generality must not be expanded without argument to every accidental-quality change.

Accidental form is not the perfection of things and does not give them being; every accidental form needs a substantial form. Essential/substantial are closely placed here, but no complete critical terminology system is independently established. Only the accidental-to-substantial prerequisite direction is written; the converse is not licensed merely by it, but this passage does not separately demonstrate substantial existence without every accident.

Each form is said to be simpler, more actual and nobler than matter. Matter must be disposed/arrayed for the form to be impressed; making fire from earth requires making the earth subtle, purified and simpler. The text supplies a requirement, not a demonstrated sufficient modern recipe.

Form makes matter known, and matter causes visible made things; matter is therefore common/general yet unknown. Matter is never seen without form and form is not seen in act except joined to matter. Do not turn mutual manifestation into symmetric ontological dependence or claim neither can be conceptually distinguished.

Adjacent82 qualifies elementary simplicity;594 already retains that context. Other chapter materials have historically qualified identities and capacities; no seamless modern ontology across the anthology is assumed.
